question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
method: best-api-review/history-v3; repeated reporter-contradiction recovery; redesign-from-first-principles hard-cut comparison
trigger: TaskHub #46 reporter contradiction against pushed commit 84bff82d4c: toolbar and typing can work, but inactive selection is activated incorrectly after the projected drag release and text input still fails intermittently.
requirements: Inactive selection may render only after focus actually transfers from the Editable to a marked keep-selection-visible control.
A blur relatedTarget is evidence about an intended transfer, not authority to activate presentation or selection side-effect suppression before focusin.
The projected drag handoff must remain able to export its collapsed native caret while the editor still owns focus.
Marked controls must continue to retain the live model selection after they genuinely receive focus.
The reporter owns browser replay; source and unit proof must not claim the intermittent native input failure is closed.
evidenceReuse: Retains the projected-selection native caret and root-interaction DOM-export handoff selected by the previous two reviews. Reopens only the prior instruction to keep inactive-selection lifecycle unchanged because the new reporter evidence and an owner-level red test show that eager blur.relatedTarget activation can enter the inactive policy before any marked control receives focus.
summary: Pursue deleting predictive inactive-selection activation from blur.relatedTarget. Blur leaves the originating store pending; only the existing document focusin observer may activate it after a marked control genuinely receives focus, so a canceled or transient transfer cannot paint inactivity or suppress the projected caret handoff.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: Root interaction must still delegate projected drag DOM selection to the existing export owner and must not clear the native range independently.

reconciliation.question: Which focus and navigation guarantees must hold for voids, owned controls, inactive editors and read-only views?
reconciliation.reason: The prior review kept inactive-selection consumers outside the repair, but the reporter contradiction and deterministic red show its eager activation is an upstream selection-policy owner, not a downstream paint-only consumer.

alternatives: Keep eager blur.relatedTarget activation and clear it from root interaction or selection export: rejected because it makes selection owners compensate for presentation state and preserves the race that blocks their work.
Hide inactive paint or ignore its policy from the floating toolbar and text-input callers: rejected because multiple consumers would disagree while the store remains falsely active.
Delete inactive selection entirely: rejected because genuinely focused marked controls need one retained selection representation while the Editable is inactive.

Defer the store on blur and activate only from the existing document focusin observer when its composed path contains the marker: chosen because one lifecycle owner observes the real focus transfer without a timer, new state, or public API.
proofLimits: The owner-level contract fails on the prior eager activation and passes when blur remains pending until focusin; existing marked-control behavior and 103 affected Plite React contracts pass. Per the reporter's instruction no browser is launched, so native event ordering, stable inactivity paint, and intermittent first-key behavior remain delegated and open.
